page: OVHcloud t1-le-90 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The hardware layout features an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor delivering 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.0 GHz without hyperthreading. System memory comprises 90.0 GB of RAM, equating to 5.62 GB per CPU core. Hardware acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs providing a combined total of 32 GB VRAM. Local storage includes a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and external connectivity is provisioned with a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary.

Benchmark results highlight strong machine learning capabilities alongside modest general-purpose compute metrics. The dual V100 configuration ranks in the top 10% for large language model inference across small and medium parameter architectures, achieving 1,311.01 tokens per second for prompt processing and 117.01 tokens per second for generation on 7B models. When scaling to 70B parameter models, prompt processing drops to an average 16.88 tokens per second due to the 32 GB aggregate VRAM boundary. Multi-core performance is average across benchmarks such as stress-ng (17,625.42) and Geekbench (6,303.0), whereas single-thread metrics fall in the bottom 25% due to the conservative per-core clock architecture.

The hardware configuration provides balanced resource efficiency for parallelized acceleration rather than heavy single-threaded compute tasks. Local NVMe SSD storage ensures rapid data retrieval for batch inference datasets, while the moderate 4 Gbps network limit can constrain ultra-large model streaming or distributed multi-node clusters. The instance fits deep learning inference on models up to 13B parameters, computer vision batch jobs, Ray tracing workloads, and mid-sized GPU-based AI pipelines.
description: OVHcloud t1-le-90 is a GPU-focused cloud instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores from an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, 90.0 GB of system memory, and dual NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs supplying 32 GB of total VRAM. Storage is bundled with a fast 400 GB NVMe SSD, alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network profile. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates standout capabilities in AI inference, scoring in the top tier for prompt evaluation and token generation on small and medium parameter models. However, single-thread CPU benchmarks register in the bottom quartile, and memory bandwidth is moderate. This makes the configuration cost-efficient for parallelized GPU compute, computer vision pipelines, medium-scale deep learning inference, and graphics rendering, while remaining constrained for heavy single-threaded compute or multi-node clustering requiring expansive network throughput.
